title: Is Grep All You Need? How Agent Harnesses Reshape Agentic Search

visual_explainer.question: How much of an apparent retriever advantage is actually caused by the surrounding agent harness and the way tool results are delivered?
visual_explainer.takeaway: Retriever ranking can flip when the same model/retrieval method is placed in a different harness or when results move from inline context to programmatic file delivery.
visual_explainer.compared_with: Studies that compare retrievers while holding the agent harness/tool-delivery path implicit.

analysis.tldr: A factorial grep-versus-vector study shows that agent harness and tool-result delivery can shift or even reverse retriever rankings, making the harness part of the causal system rather than implementation detail.
analysis.problem: Agentic retrieval papers often attribute outcome differences to the retriever while changing prompts, tool schemas, result rendering, file access, and stopping behavior through the surrounding harness.
analysis.core_idea: Cross lexical versus vector retrieval with multiple harnesses and two delivery modes—inline tool output versus programmatic file-based reading—on the same LongMemEval-S questions.
analysis.agent_loop: query → harness schedules retrieval tool → results delivered inline or via file → model inspects evidence → continue/answer
analysis.retrieval_design: The paper does not propose a new retriever; it treats retrieval mode × harness × delivery path as interacting experimental factors.
analysis.evidence: On the 116-question LongMemEval-S subset, inline grep beats inline vector for every tested harness-model pair, but programmatic delivery reverses the ordering on five of ten pairs. For GPT-5.4 in Codex, grep drops from 93.1% with inline delivery to 55.2% with programmatic delivery, while programmatic vector reaches 67.2%. The same Claude Opus 4.6 model reaches 93.1% under Chronos grep and 76.7% under Claude Code grep.
analysis.why_it_matters: This raises the evaluation bar for Agentic RAG: retriever comparisons are not interpretable unless the harness and evidence-delivery path are controlled or explicitly factorized.
limitations: The benchmark is long-memory conversational QA with many literal witnesses, which may favor lexical retrieval.
Provider harnesses differ in several coupled behaviors, so the study diagnoses a confound more cleanly than it isolates one harness mechanism.
Some scaling comparisons remain incomplete or stack-specific.
